same-toy.title: The same toy
same-toy.skill: Ask for a turn and respect the current turn
needs: I want to play with the car
I want to finish the garage
same-toy.coach: Ask each partner what they need. A child does not have to lend a personal toy. Agree on an ending signal; waiting is not a punishment.
same-toy.easier: Act out both parts with toys. Show one option at a time.
same-toy.harder: Ask the partners to suggest another ending signal and review it.
steps: Sami is playing with the red car. Layan wants it too. Can they find a plan without grabbing?
Layan says: I want to play. Sami says: I want to finish the garage. Let us hear both needs.
Ask calmly: May I have a turn when you finish? Choose the need you want to act out.
Agree on an ending signal, or play with two cars. Choose a plan that suits you both. You can ask for another idea.
Try the plan with real toys or puppets. Then choose: We tried our agreement.
Did the plan suit you both? Keep it, change it, or take a break.

solutions.title: Finish, then offer a turn
solutions.rule: Finish the garage, then offer the car when the current player is ready.
solutions.text: Agree on the end of the turn. When the car enters the garage, Sami offers Layan a turn. We do not grab.

solutions.title: Two cars and two roads
solutions.rule: Choose two cars and play together without having to swap personal toys.
solutions.text: Each child chooses a car and a road. Play together without a forced swap. Change the plan if it does not feel right.

change-rule.title: Shall we change the rule?
change-rule.skill: Try a rule change and review how it works
needs: I want a distance I can manage
change-rule.coach: Changing a rule is a shared decision. Ask whether both partners can join comfortably. A challenge is not a ranking of children.
change-rule.easier: Use a soft ball and a nearby basket. Act out the two choices.
change-rule.harder: Test both choices and explain which part made participation easier.
steps: Omar wants the basket farther away. Hana wants a distance she can manage. Can they change the rule together?
Omar wants a challenge. Hana wants a comfortable way to join. Both needs matter.
Ask: Can we test the new distance together before deciding?
Try a short test round, or let each player choose a suitable distance. Explore both plans.
Try your chosen rule with a soft ball or act it out with toys. Then confirm that you tried it.
Did everyone get to join? Keep the rule or change one part and test again.

solutions.title: A short test round
solutions.rule: Try the changed distance for a short round, then decide together.
solutions.text: Try the new distance in a short round. Afterwards, ask each partner whether the change suited them.

solutions.title: A distance for each player
solutions.rule: Each player chooses a suitable distance. Nobody is mocked for their choice.
solutions.text: Choose a suitable distance for each player. A fair game can include different distances. Ask whether the plan feels right to everyone.

new-player.title: A new player joins us
new-player.skill: Find a real, freely chosen role for a new partner
needs: I want to join the building
We want to keep our bridge safe
new-player.coach: Ask what role the new player wants. Give a useful job rather than a token place. Joining and continuing are voluntary.
new-player.easier: Use three toys and one clear building job.
new-player.harder: Rotate the roles and ask each partner what changed.
steps: Adam and Reem are building a bridge. Zaid wants to join. Can they find a useful role without knocking down the work?
Zaid wants to help build. Adam and Reem want to keep their bridge safe. Listen to both needs.
Ask: What can I build with you? Show me which part needs help.
Zaid could build the road or another part of the bridge. Ask what he would like to try.
Build a small part together, then test the bridge with a toy car. Confirm only after you try.
Did Zaid have a useful role? Did everyone agree? Change the jobs if needed.

solutions.title: Build the road
solutions.rule: Zaid builds the road and connects it to the bridge after checking with the group.
solutions.text: Zaid chooses to build the road. Show where it meets the bridge and leave him a real building job. Ask whether it suits him.

solutions.title: Build part of the bridge
solutions.rule: Zaid builds an agreed part of the bridge, and the group tests it together.
solutions.text: Choose a part of the bridge that Zaid wants to build. Explain how it connects. Then the group tests the car together.
